_comment: Self-Compassion Scale (SCS), Neff, K. D. (2003). Development and validation of a scale to measure self-compassion. Self and Identity, 2, 223-250. Full 26-item long form plus the official 6-subscale scoring key, taken verbatim from the author's own distributed scale PDF (self-compassion.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/SCS-information.pdf, fetched 2026-10-19), which grants explicit permission ('Dr. Kristin Neff grants permission to use the Self-Compassion Scale (Neff, 2003) for any purpose whatsoever, including research...'). Registered per 12.gdx.virtology/GoDataX_H7ph_33_Virtudes_Instrumentos_Psicometricos.xlsx, which suggests SCS for 'Aceitacao' (Mindfulness/Common Humanity), 'Tudo Somos Um' (Common Humanity), 'Nao Julgamento' (Mindfulness/Self-Judgment) and 'Desapego' (IPIP-Modesty; SCS-Mindfulness). The full validated 6-subscale instrument is loaded faithfully (all 26 items, all 6 subscales) even though only 3 subscales (Mindfulness, Common Humanity, Self-Judgment) end up associated to a virtue -- Self-Kindness, Isolation and Over-Identification are cataloged but not virtue-mapped in this batch. IMPORTANT scoring note: per the official key, subscale scores are the MEAN of their items (not the sum), and Self-Judgment, Isolation and Over-Identification are the SCALE's own negative-pole subscales (GDX_PSY_INDICATOR.DIRECTION stays POSITIVE here since a high raw score literally means 'more of the construct as named', e.g. more self-judgment -- the SCALE_POLARITY column in GDX_VT_VARIABLE_VIRTUE_MAP is what will flag these as undesirable when associated to a virtue, same convention already used for the existing 'Negative Emotions' row in that table). Catalog registration only -- no participant data collected or associated with this record.

study.title: Self-Compassion Scale (SCS) - Instrument Onboarding
study.objective: Register the full Self-Compassion Scale (Neff, 2003), all 6 subscales, as the source instrument for the Virtology virtues Aceitacao, Tudo Somos Um, Nao Julgamento and Desapego, per GoDataX_H7ph_33_Virtudes_Instrumentos_Psicometricos.xlsx.
study.method: Official scale text and scoring key, self-compassion.org (Neff, 2003); catalog registration only, no primary data collection associated with this record.

instruments.name: Self-Compassion Scale (SCS)
instruments.description: Neff, K. D. (2003). Development and validation of a scale to measure self-compassion. Self and Identity, 2, 223-250. Full 26-item long form, 6 subscales (Self-Kindness, Self-Judgment, Common Humanity, Isolation, Mindfulness, Over-Identification). Free to use for any purpose per the author's own distributed permission letter.
instruments.instructions: HOW I TYPICALLY ACT TOWARDS MYSELF IN DIFFICULT TIMES. Please read each statement carefully before answering. For each item, indicate how often you behave in the stated manner, using the 1-5 scale below. Please answer according to what really reflects your experience rather than what you think your experience should be.
instruments.phenomenon_description: Being kind and understanding toward oneself in instances of pain or failure; perceiving one's own experiences as part of the larger human experience; holding painful thoughts and feelings in mindful awareness rather than over-identifying with them (Neff, 2003).

constructs.name: Self-Kindness (SCS)
constructs.definition: Being warm and understanding toward oneself in instances of pain or failure, rather than being harshly self-critical.

constructs.name: Self-Judgment (SCS)
constructs.definition: Being disapproving and judgmental toward one's own flaws and inadequacies, rather than kind and understanding (the negative pole of Self-Kindness).

constructs.name: Common Humanity (SCS)
constructs.definition: Seeing one's own imperfections and failures as part of the shared human experience, rather than as something that isolates one from others.

constructs.name: Isolation (SCS)
constructs.definition: Feeling cut off and separated from the rest of the world by one's own suffering and inadequacy (the negative pole of Common Humanity).

constructs.name: Mindfulness (SCS)
constructs.definition: Holding one's painful thoughts and feelings in balanced awareness, rather than over-identifying with them.

constructs.name: Over-Identification (SCS)
constructs.definition: Becoming consumed by and fused with one's negative emotions and thoughts about oneself (the negative pole of Mindfulness).

items.statement_text: I'm disapproving and judgmental about my own flaws and inadequacies.
When I'm feeling down I tend to obsess and fixate on everything that's wrong.
When things are going badly for me, I see the difficulties as part of life that everyone goes through.
When I think about my inadequacies, it tends to make me feel more separate and cut off from the rest of the world.
I try to be loving towards myself when I'm feeling emotional pain.
When I fail at something important to me I become consumed by feelings of inadequacy.
When I'm down, I remind myself that there are lots of other people in the world feeling like I am.
When times are really difficult, I tend to be tough on myself.
When something upsets me I try to keep my emotions in balance.
When I feel inadequate in some way, I try to remind myself that feelings of inadequacy are shared by most people.
I'm intolerant and impatient towards those aspects of my personality I don't like.
When I'm going through a very hard time, I give myself the caring and tenderness I need.
When I'm feeling down, I tend to feel like most other people are probably happier than I am.
When something painful happens I try to take a balanced view of the situation.
I try to see my failings as part of the human condition.
When I see aspects of myself that I don't like, I get down on myself.
When I fail at something important to me I try to keep things in perspective.
When I'm really struggling, I tend to feel like other people must be having an easier time of it.
I'm kind to myself when I'm experiencing suffering.
When something upsets me I get carried away with my feelings.
I can be a bit cold-hearted towards myself when I'm experiencing suffering.
When I'm feeling down I try to approach my feelings with curiosity and openness.
I'm tolerant of my own flaws and inadequacies.
When something painful happens I tend to blow the incident out of proportion.
When I fail at something that's important to me, I tend to feel alone in my failure.
I try to be understanding and patient towards those aspects of my personality I don't like.
